sentences.text: That on 19.06.2024 at about 2.30 PM, near K.Narayanapura main road, wherein she was crossing the said road, wherein the driver of the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-03-KP-5320, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.

In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she was shifted to Cratis Hospital then she was shifted to CMI Aster Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuriews.
Petitioner has spent Rs.4,30,000/- towards her medical expenses.
Petitioner stated that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to perform her work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the she was hale and healthy and she is aged about 23 years and she was doing program Anlyst at Manyatha Tech park and thereby she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent no.1 who insured his vehicle with respondent no.2 and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.74/2024 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
As such both are liable to pay compensation and he prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they have appeared through their counsel and filed vakalath.

Respondent No.2 filed the written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioner in toto and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to file the written statement, hence his written statement is taken as not filed.

4. Petitioner examined herself as PW-1 and got marked 14 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 14 and she is fully cross examined and respondent no.2 examined its legal manager as RW-1 and marked 3 documents which are at Ex.R1 to 3 and she is fully cross examined.
5.
I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.

Counsel appearing for respondent NO.2 has relied on following authorities:
1. Mahaveer Vs The Branch Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd., and others - SLP No.11557/2025.
2. TATA GIC Ltd., VS Manjunatha and others - MFA No.7018/2023 C/w 2658/2024.
In MFA 7018/2023.
6.

On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES Thanushreen N Alias Thanushree N Gowda vs Abdul Basith on 5 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153659011/
2 1.Whether the petitioner proves that on 19.06.2024 at about 2.30 PM, near K.Narayanapura main road, wherein she was crossing the said road, wherein the driver of the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA-03-KP-5320, drove it with high speed,
rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.

entities.text: ISSUES Thanushreen N Alias Thanushree N Gowda vs Abdul Basith
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition.?
2)Whether respondent No.2 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions as contended in the written statement.?
3.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?
PW1 being the petitioner, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, sketch, wound certificate, final report and wound certificate, IMV report, which are at Ex.P.1 to 6 and 11.
9. On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that is one Ifzal Ahmed.
S S / o Arrif is the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
Ex.P.8 is the reply notice given by the respondent No.1 to the notice issued by the police under section 133 of M.V.Act.
It reveals that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving license as on the date of the accident.
Further Ex.P.11 is the final report filed against the respondent No.1 and the driver of the offending vehicle, Ex.P.6 is the IMV report.
The aforesaid documents establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and respondent No.1.

The final report filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
In the cross examination of PW-1, she admitted that there was no zebra crossing mark in the way/path trough which she crossed the road.

She admit that she has received compensation amount of Rs.2,80,000/- from the health insurance company and she is working in the company and drawing the same salary as earlier.

sentences.text: Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, as per Ex.P5 and inpatient bill as per Ex.P13.

The aforesaid documents establishes that she has sustained grievous injuries that is right zygomatic maxillary fracture and its fixation was done under GA on 21.06.2024 and she has taken treatment as an inpatient for 6 days and she has incurred the medical expenditure as stated in Ex.P.13 that is Rs.2,24,999/- it is also true that out of the said amount petitioner has paid Rs.35,000/- and balance amount is paid by the Health insurance company as admitted by the PW-1 and she has paid the premium for the said health insurance policy.
Further petitioner has not examined the treated doctor and she has not whispered the physical or functional disability.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, Medicines,
Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
11.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the treatment taken by her for the accidental injuries as noted in wound certificate.
Admittedly she has taken treatment for 6 days as inpatient, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, she might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.2,24,999/-, I award Rs.20,000/-.
In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,44,999/- compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
12. The petitioner has not substantiated the established his nature of his work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as her monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least one month, he has lost his income.

Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- X 1 month =
Rs. 16,500/- as compensation under this head.
13. Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
Admittedly the petitioner has not examined the doctor who treated her nor she whispered the physical or functional disability.
Admittedly petitioner is working and drawing same salary as earlier.
Accordingly she is not entitled for compensation under this head.
14.NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES: (General Damages) (IV) Damages for Pain & sufferings and Trauma as a consequence of the injuries :-

The petitioner has undergone pain and sufferings during the accident and during the rehabilitation period, therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.
V) Loss of Amenities :-
15.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for her before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.

sentences.text: Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
Sl No.
Particulars

Amount 1 Towards medical expenses Rs.2,44,999/-
2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 16,500/-
3 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
4 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.3,01,499/-
17.
Rate of Interest:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s
Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.a.
Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.a. on the compensation am 18.
Liability :
The respondent no.1 is the insurer of offending vehicle and the validity of the said policy is not in disputed.
Admittedly as per final report, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving license as on the date of the accident and admittedly he has violated the policy conditions.
Accordingly respondent no.2 has established its contention that respondent no.1 has violated the policy condition.

Further more the abstinence of respondent No.1 before the tribunal probabilise that he has accepted his actionable negligent act and his guilt and it further establishes that accident occurred due to his sole negligent act, for that insurer cannot be made liable.

With great respect to the authorities relied on by the respondent No.2 and by considering the principles laid down therein, and by considering the facts and attending circumstance of the present case and the conduct of the respondent No.1, this tribunal is of firm conclusion that respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation for his negligence act.
Accordingly liability cannot be fastened to the respondent No.2 for the negligent act of the respondent No.1 and the driver of his vehicle.
Accordingly respondent no.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest.
Accordingly respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 30 days of judgment.
Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 and 2 in the affirmative and issue No.3 in partly affirmative.
19. Issue No.4:

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.3,01,499/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
